deals.handout: South has a weak hand with 5+ hearts. South transfers to 2♥ and passes.

problems.explanation: With six hearts and only 3 HCP, 2♥ will play better than 1NT. Bid 2♦, a Jacoby transfer, and pass partner's 2♥. Partner declares, so the lead comes up to the strong hand.

whyNot.P: 1NT opposite 3 HCP and a singleton diamond will struggle. Your six hearts play better as trumps.
whyNot.2H: 2♥ is a transfer to spades. To show hearts, bid 2♦.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2♦ is a Jacoby transfer: five or more hearts, any strength. You must complete it by bidding 2♥, whatever you hold there.

whyNot.P: The transfer is forcing. Partner may have no diamonds at all.
whyNot.2N: Complete the transfer with 2♥. Partner will tell you more if they have more.

problems.explanation: Partner completed the transfer. You have 0–7 points, so pass: you've reached a better partscore than 1NT.

whyNot.3H: Bidding 3♥ invites game, showing 8–9. You have 3.
whyNot.2N: 2NT invites game, showing 8–9 and five hearts. You have 3.

deals.handout: With 6 hearts, North should transfer to 2♥ and then raise to 3♥. This bid shows 8 or 9 points and at least a 6 card suit.
reviewNotes: North has 7 HCP, where the lesson says to transfer and pass. The handout invites with 3♥, so that's the answer; passing is marked acceptable.

problems.explanation: You have six hearts. Whatever your strength, start with 2♦, a Jacoby transfer, so partner declares the heart contract.

whyNot.2H: 2♥ is a transfer to spades. To show hearts, bid 2♦.
whyNot.P: With six hearts, a heart contract will play better than 1NT.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2♦ is a Jacoby transfer: five or more hearts, any strength. You must complete it by bidding 2♥, whatever you hold there.

whyNot.3H: Just complete the transfer. Partner will invite if they want to.

acceptable.P: By the lesson's point ranges, 7 HCP is a pass. The handout invites anyway, counting the sixth heart.

problems.explanation: You have six hearts and the transfer is done. Raise to 3♥: an invitation with a six-card suit. Partner bids 4♥ with a maximum.

whyNot.4H: Opposite 15–17, game needs more than you have. Invite.
whyNot.2N: 2NT shows exactly five hearts. With six, raise hearts.

problems.explanation: Partner's 3♥ invites with six hearts. You have three hearts and a maximum, 17, so bid 4♥.

whyNot.P: With 17, a maximum, accept the invitation.
whyNot.3N: Partner has six hearts and you have three: play in hearts.

deals.handout: North doubles 2♥ to ask for a heart lead. East passes over the double to show fewer than 3 spades. With 11 points and a heart stopper West bids 3 NT.

problems.explanation: You have five spades and 11 HCP: enough for game. Bid 2♥, a Jacoby transfer, then 3NT, so partner can choose between 3NT and 4♠.

whyNot.3N: Partner may have three spades. Transfer first, then bid 3NT and let partner choose.
whyNot.4S: Partner may have only two spades. Transfer, then bid 3NT.

problems.explanation: West's 2♥ is artificial: a transfer to spades. A double asks partner to lead hearts. With KJ1094 you'd like a heart lead, so double.

whyNot.P: You want partner to lead a heart. The double tells them.

problems.explanation: Partner's transfer was doubled. You have only two spades, so pass to say so. With three or more, you'd bid 2♠.

whyNot.2S: Over the double, accepting the transfer shows three or more spades. You have two.

problems.explanation: Partner's pass says only two spades, so there's no 5-3 fit. You have game values and a heart stopper (the ♥A), so bid 3NT.

whyNot.2S: You have game values. Bid game.
whyNot.4S: Partner has only two spades. 3NT is the better game.

deals.handout: East transfers to hearts when he bids 2♦. His rebid of 2 NT shows exactly five hearts and 8-9 high-card points. Since West is at the top of his bid and holds three hearts, he accepts the invitation by jumping to 4♥.

problems.explanation: You have five hearts and 8 HCP. Bid 2♦, a Jacoby transfer, then 2NT to invite.

whyNot.2N: 2NT invites, but partner can't tell you have five hearts. Transfer first.
whyNot.2H: 2♥ is a transfer to spades. To show hearts, bid 2♦.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2♦ is a Jacoby transfer: five or more hearts, any strength. You must complete it by bidding 2♥, whatever you hold there.
You have exactly five hearts and 8–9 points. Bid 2NT: an invitation that shows five hearts. Partner chooses between pass, 3♥, 3NT and 4♥.

whyNot.3H: Raising to 3♥ shows six hearts. You have five.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2NT shows five hearts and 8–9 points. You have three hearts and a maximum, 17, so bid 4♥.

whyNot.3H: 3♥ shows three hearts but a minimum. With 17, bid game.
whyNot.3N: With three hearts, play in the 5-3 heart fit.
whyNot.P: With 17, a maximum, accept the invitation.

deals.handout: West has a very weak hand with long spades. West transfers to spades and passes 3♠.

problems.explanation: Jacoby transfers work over 2NT too, one level higher. With six spades and 1 HCP, 3♠ will play better than 2NT. Bid 3♥, a transfer, and pass 3♠.

whyNot.P: 2NT opposite 1 HCP will struggle. Your spades play better as trumps.
whyNot.3S: 3♠ would be natural and forcing. Transfer with 3♥ and pass.

problems.explanation: Partner's 3♥ is a Jacoby transfer over 2NT: five or more spades. Complete it with 3♠.
Partner completed the transfer. With almost nothing, pass.

whyNot.4S: You have 1 HCP. Game is unlikely.

deals.handout: Transfers still apply after a 2♣ overcall, or after a double but not after an overcall of 2D or above. In order to show a game forcing hand with 5 hearts, North jumps to 3♥. South has a fit and raises to game.

problems.explanation: Over a 2♦ overcall, transfers are off and you bid naturally. With five hearts and game values, jump to 3♥: forcing, so partner chooses 4♥ or 3NT.

whyNot.2H: Over the overcall, 2♥ is natural and weak (0–7). You have game values.
whyNot.4H: You have only five hearts. Let partner choose between 4♥ and 3NT.
whyNot.3N: With a singleton diamond and five hearts, show the hearts first.

problems.explanation: Partner's 3♥ is natural and forcing: five hearts and game values. You have three hearts, so bid 4♥.

whyNot.3N: You have three hearts, so play the 5-3 fit.

deals.handout: After North bids 2D showing a least a five card heart suit, South jumps in hearts, showing a good 1 NT opener with at least 4 hearts. North accepts the game in hearts.
reviewNotes: The Jacoby text doesn't cover opener's jump to 3♥ with four hearts. The problem follows the handout; completing the transfer with 2♥ is marked acceptable.

problems.explanation: You have six hearts. Start with 2♦, a Jacoby transfer, so partner declares the heart contract.

whyNot.2H: 2♥ is a transfer to spades. To show hearts, bid 2♦.
whyNot.P: With six hearts, a heart contract will play better than 1NT.

acceptable.2H: Completing the transfer is always fine. The jump to 3♥ shows a good hand with four hearts, which the handout teaches here.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2♦ shows five or more hearts. You have four, and a good hand, so jump to 3♥ instead of just completing the transfer. It shows four-card support and a good 1NT, and partner can bid game with less.

whyNot.4H: Partner may have nothing. 3♥ shows the fit and leaves room to stop.

problems.explanation: Partner jumped to 3♥: four hearts and a good 1NT. You have six hearts, so a ten-card fit, and 7 HCP. That's enough for game opposite this: bid 4♥.

whyNot.P: Partner's jump shows a fit and a good hand. With six hearts, bid game.

deals.handout: With 6 Spades and 9 points, East wants to play game in spades. The way to do this is to transfer to 2♠ and then bid 4♠.
reviewNotes: The Jacoby lesson came before Texas, so the handout transfers and then bids 4♠ to play game. Since learning Texas, we use Texas for game without slam interest and keep transfer-then-4♠ for slam interest. Problem 8a follows that.

problems.answerNote: The handout transfers with 2♥ and then bids 4♠, which is right without Texas. We learned Texas afterwards, and with it, transfer-then-4♠ shows slam interest, so the answer here is Texas, 4♥.
problems.explanation: You have six spades and enough for game, with no interest in slam. Bid 4♥, a Texas transfer: partner bids 4♠ and declares it.

whyNot.4S: 4♠ is the right contract, but played from the wrong side. Texas lets the strong hand declare it.
whyNot.2H: Without Texas, transferring and then bidding 4♠ is right, and it's what the handout does. But now that we play Texas, that sequence shows slam interest. With 9 HCP you have none, so use Texas.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2♥ is a Jacoby transfer: five or more spades, any strength. You must complete it by bidding 2♠, whatever you hold there.
